title: Zardari in Germany: 75 years of ties
credits: Photos: Hassan Anwer, Shujaat Muzaffar / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Pakistan's president, Asif Ali Zardari, is in Germany, as the two countries mark seventy-five years of diplomatic relations.
He left for Berlin on Thursday, for a three-day visit lasting until the twenty-fourth of October.
He is there at the invitation of Germany's president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier.
According to Geo News, it is the first visit to Germany by a Pakistani head of state in about two decades.
Pakistan's Foreign Office says the trip has a particular focus on trade and economic cooperation.
Zardari is due to meet Germany's senior leadership, and German business leaders.
Sindh's chief minister, Murad Ali Shah, is expected to join him.
In June, a German delegation announced plans to bring around thirty German companies to Pakistan.
And in September, Germany's Foreign Office praised Pakistan's mediation in regional conflicts, including over the Strait of Hormuz.
Germany is the European Union's biggest economy, which makes it a key partner for Pakistani exports.
For Islamabad, this visit is a chance to turn seventy-five years of friendship into more trade and investment.
